PHP 47 M Flood Control Project in Laoag Collapses Ties Emerge Between Contractor Linked to Davao Lawmaker and Sandro Marcos Office A newly built flood control structure along Padsan River in Barangay Gabu Laoag City a project worth PHP 47,024,704.34 funded under the 2024 General Appropriations Act GAA has collapsed JUST MONTHS after its reported completion sparking fresh outrage over the alleged flood-control mafia operating in Congress Photos taken on-site show large concrete revetments cracked dislodged and washed into the river exposing reinforcing steel and leaving the riverbank vulnerable to further erosion The project billboard names RA Pahati Construction and Supply Inc as the contractor under the DPWH Ilocos Norte First District Engineering Office with a target completion date of October 4 2024 RA Pahati Construction is reportedly owned by the family of Rep Jhong Ceniza of Pantukan Davao de Oro a name that has repeatedly surfaced in infrastructure procurement circles Sources familiar with congressional contracting allege that RA Pahati has become a favored builder for Rep Sandro Marcos the Ilocos Norte 1st District Representative allegedly with some help from his chief of staff said to be a relative of Rep Ceniza's wife Residents and local engineers have raised alarm over the collapse noting that the structure failed despite relatively moderate river flow in recent weeks Infrastructure experts point out that proper soil compaction adequate riprap foundation and correct steel reinforcement are crucial in river dike construction all of which appear deficient in the broken sections The collapse has revived long-circulating allegations about flood control allocations being used as a cash cow for certain districts RA Pahati controlled by the Ceniza family has reportedly bagged billions in contracts across Luzon and Mindanao despite originating from Davao de Oro In Ilocos Norte whispers persist that Rep Sandro Marcos chief of staff reportedly related by marriage to the Cenizas has been instrumental in channeling projects to RA Pahati bypassing stricter vetting Political analysts warn this could become a serious governance issue for the presidential son especially as calls mount for greater transparency in the use of massive DPWH flood control budgets The incident adds to the growing backlash against multi-billion flood control projects nationwide long suspected to be overpriced poorly built and politically manipulated In Congress several lawmakers particularly from Mindanao have been calling out selective investigations that spare politically allied districts while targeting rivals Observers warn that this Laoag project could become a flashpoint especially since it sits in the home turf of the President's son who is Additional Information The key difference between a Heavy Rainfall Warning and a Weather Advisory lies in their forecast period coverage areas and accuracy A Heavy Rainfall Warning provides forecasts for the next three hours and applies up to the municipal level It is more precise as it utilizes Doppler radar technology to track real-time rainfall intensity making it highly effective for immediate decision-making in flood-prone areas A Weather Advisory on the other hand covers a 24 hour period but is issued only at the provincial level It provides a broader outlook on potential weather disturbances but lacks the short-term accuracy of Heavy Rainfall Warnings Since a Weather Advisory is based on a 24 hour outlook it should not be used as a basis for class suspensions or other official decisions Source DOST-Pagasa Weather Advisory No 1
